name: Outbreak of the Hundred Years War
summary: The Hundred Years War began in 1337 when Philip VI of France confiscated the English Duchy of Gascony and Edward III of England responded by claiming the French throne (through his mother Isabella). The war grew from a feudal dispute over Gascony into a contest over French sovereignty itself. Over 116 years it transformed both kingdoms: France developed a professional army and national identity; England's defeat produced the Wars of the Roses.
outcomes: French succession dispute becomes full war
England and France at war intermittently until 1453

_quarry.structural_significance: The defining conflict of late medieval Western Europe; it created the conditions for French national monarchy and contributed to the political instability that produced the Tudor and Valois dynasties.
